questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: A phone app that offers mental health therapy
How robots are built in Star Wars films
Why therapists are too expensive
How to protect your privacy online when using health apps
questions.why: They discuss Woebot, an app in your smartphone that talks to you as a kind of therapist.

options: It was named after its inventor
It is a joke, because 'woe' means sadness
It means 'robot' in another language
It was the name of a film character
questions.why: Rob says 'Woe means sadness; so this is a woe bot, not a robot', showing its sense of humour.

questions.q: According to Dr Alison Darcy, what does Woebot do every day?
options: Sends you articles to read
Books appointments with doctors and therapists near your home
Asks how you are and offers to talk things through
Records your sleep
questions.why: She says he'll check in with you every day and ask 'How do you feel?'

questions.q: What have trials of Woebot shown?
options: It is better than a real therapist for most kinds of problems
It doesn't work at all
It works only for young people
It can work better than just reading about mental health
questions.why: Catherine says trials show it can be more effective than simply reading information about mental health.

questions.q: Why haven't researchers compared Woebot with a real therapist?
options: It would be wrong to deny patients a human therapist
It would cost too much
The therapists they asked all refused to take part in the trial
There weren't enough patients
questions.why: Rob says it could be unethical to deny a real patient access to a human therapist for a trial.

questions.q: What other worry about apps like this is mentioned?
options: They use too much battery
They are too difficult to use
Users aren't protected by strong privacy laws
They sometimes give dangerous advice to people who are ill
questions.why: Catherine says people using such apps 'are not protected by strong privacy laws'.

questions.q: Why does Dr Darcy say people have little time for self-reflection today?
options: They work too many hours
Their phones always fill quiet moments
They sleep too little
They travel too much
questions.why: She says even a commute can now be filled with content 'by looking at your phone'.

questions.q: What does Catherine say about trying a therapy app herself?
options: She would never try it
She would only try it with a doctor
She has already tried it and didn't like it
She would try it and thinks it could help
questions.why: She says 'Yes I would, actually – I think it might be quite helpful.'
